webshop.description: Search a simulated online shop and buy a product that meets a shopper’s requirements.
webshop.input: Shopping request and simulated online store
webshop.output: Searches, page actions and final product selection
webshop.assessment: Reward for matching requested attributes, options and price
webshop.first_author_affil: Department of Computer Science, Princeton University

api-bank.description: Determine when to find and call an API, execute it and respond in the ongoing dialogue.
api-bank.input: User dialogue, API descriptions and execution environment
api-bank.output: API calls and follow-up dialogue responses
api-bank.assessment: API-call correctness; ROUGE-L for follow-up responses

mind2web.description: Predict each next action from demonstrations of real websites, rather than driving a live browser.
mind2web.input: Task, webpage snapshot and action history
mind2web.output: Target element, operation and optional value
mind2web.assessment: Element accuracy, operation F1 and step/task success

webarena.description: Complete instructions on working replicas of websites; check what actually changed on the site.
webarena.input: User goal and an interactive replica website
webarena.output: Browser actions and, when requested, a written answer
webarena.assessment: Task-specific checks on page state, URL or answer

toolbench.description: Resolve user requests by planning and executing API calls; compare the resulting solution paths.
toolbench.input: User instruction and available API documentation
toolbench.assessment: ToolEval model judges task pass rate and pairwise wins

agentbench.description: Operate in multiple environments, from databases to games; each environment defines its own objective.
agentbench.input: Task, environment state and available actions
agentbench.output: Sequence of environment-specific actions or responses
agentbench.assessment: Environment-specific success or reward, then aggregate scoring

gaia.description: Answer practical questions that require combinations of browsing, file handling, tools and reasoning.
gaia.input: Real-world question, sometimes with an attached file
gaia.assessment: Normalized final answer matched against the reference

webvoyager.description: Complete user requests across live websites. WebVoyager names both the original agent and the evaluation; this entry is the evaluation.
webvoyager.input: A user request and annotated browser screenshots in the visual setting
webvoyager.output: Browser actions and a final answer
webvoyager.assessment: Task success rate; distinguish human judgments from the automated visual judge.

bfcl.description: Select a function and its arguments, handle parallel calls, or withhold a call when none fits.
bfcl.input: User request and available function signatures
bfcl.output: Function calls with arguments, or no call
bfcl.assessment: Syntax-tree matching or execution checks by category
bfcl.date_note: First leaderboard announcement. Later paper and leaderboard versions are separate events.

osworld.description: Operate real desktop applications and verify the resulting operating-system or application state.
osworld.input: Natural-language instruction and initialized desktop environment
osworld.output: Desktop actions that change applications or files
osworld.assessment: Task-specific execution checks on the resulting state
osworld.date_note: Existing entry and stable slug; bare family labels need source context before assigning an edition result.

androidworld.description: Complete a task in Android apps. The environment checks the device state, not whether an action sequence matches a demonstration.
androidworld.input: A user instruction and a configured Android device
androidworld.output: UI actions that complete the requested task
androidworld.assessment: Task-specific checks of the resulting device state
androidworld.date_note: Original paper v1; distinct from Android in the Wild and OSWorld.

tau-bench.description: Converse with a simulated customer and call tools; check the final database state against the goal.
tau-bench.input: Simulated customer, domain policy, tools and database
tau-bench.output: Tool actions and messages to the customer
tau-bench.assessment: Final database state and required reply contents checked

browsecomp.description: Search the web for a hard-to-locate fact and return a short, verifiable answer.
browsecomp.input: A question and access to the web
browsecomp.assessment: Answer correctness against a reference, using the documented grader
browsecomp.date_note: Public launch of the original BrowseComp. Other language editions and long-context adaptations have separate protocols.

toolathlon.description: Carry out a request by coordinating tools across applications. The final Verified release revised prompts, checks and reference outcomes.
toolathlon.input: A task and an initialized software workspace
toolathlon.output: Tool actions and a completed workspace task
toolathlon.first_author_affil: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

automationbench.description: Complete a business workflow across simulated SaaS systems and respect its policies.
automationbench.input: Business request and starting application state
automationbench.output: Tool actions and final state across apps
automationbench.assessment: Assertions check outcomes and policy compliance
automationbench.date_note: Zapier launch. AutomationBench-AA is an independently administered evaluation; the Zapier leaderboard uses a harder held-out set. Neither is a separate spelling of a new matrix cell.

harness-bench.description: Run the same workflow tasks with different model–harness pairs. Hold tasks and budgets fixed to see what changes when the tools and execution framework change.
harness-bench.input: Task instructions and workspace materials; some tasks in the expanded suite include images
harness-bench.output: Completed work products and changes to the task workspace
harness-bench.assessment: Task-specific checkers score the delivered work. Record the model, harness, task set and budget with the result.
harness-bench.date_note: First paper on Harness-Bench. The project also publishes an expanded task suite; compare results from the same suite and budget.

tau2-bench.description: Coordinate with a simulated user who can also change the environment. The original τ² release adds a dual-control telecom domain.
tau2-bench.input: A support request, domain policies, tools and a simulated user
tau2-bench.output: A conversation and tool actions that complete the task
tau2-bench.assessment: End-state checks and required outputs; pass^k measures consistent success across repeated attempts.
tau2-bench.date_note: Sierra announcement. This is not the October 2026 release called τ-bench 2.0.0.

alternative_dates.note: arXiv v1 submission before the June 10 announcement.

tau2-bench-0-1-3.description: A τ² revision that removes default natural-language assertion checks. Specify the grading version when comparing results that depend on those checks.
tau2-bench-0-1-3.input: A policy, support request and interactive tool environment
tau2-bench-0-1-3.assessment: State and tool checks under the 0.1.3 defaults; natural-language assertions no longer run by default.
tau2-bench-0-1-3.date_note: GitHub published release; the changelog documents the grading default.

tau3-bench.description: Extend agent–user tasks to support-document retrieval and real-time spoken interaction. This public suite corresponds to repository release v1.0.0.
tau3-bench.input: A text or spoken support request, domain tools and policies or a knowledge base
tau3-bench.output: A response and effective changes in the customer-support environment
tau3-bench.assessment: Task-specific completion checks and repeated-run reliability, reported by domain and interface.
tau3-bench.date_note: Sierra announcement and matching GitHub release; not the original 2024 τ-bench.

tau-bench-1-0-1.description: A grading revision to the τ³ generation. It corrects banking knowledge task data and evaluation; the authors say the other domains are unaffected.
tau-bench-1-0-1.input: A support interaction with domain tools; banking tasks also have a policy corpus
tau-bench-1-0-1.assessment: Revised banking task and rubric checks. Pre-1.0.1 banking scores are not directly comparable.
tau-bench-1-0-1.date_note: Public GitHub release dated July 22 UTC. Some fixes reached main on July 14–15 without a version bump; this row dates the named release, not an individual fix.

tau-bench-2-0-0.description: Evaluate text and voice interactions across languages using pinned task manifests. The official release changes task prompts, judging and caller configuration.
tau-bench-2-0-0.input: A text or voice support request, domain tools and a language-specific environment
tau-bench-2-0-0.output: A dialogue and task-specific environment updates
tau-bench-2-0-0.assessment: Completion and consistency on the named text or voice manifest; 1.x scores are not interchangeable.

alternative_dates.note: GitHub published_at is Oct 20 00:28 UTC. The release body and dated changelog state October 19.

agents-last-exam.description: Complete multi-step professional workflows across real software environments.
agents-last-exam.input: A workplace task, tools and domain-specific software
agents-last-exam.output: A completed task artifact and application state
agents-last-exam.assessment: Task-specific verifiers assess the resulting work on the corresponding release.

agents-last-exam-1-1.description: The finalized v1.1 scope has 122 active tasks after 30 retirements. It revises task instructions, environments, verification and data for selected workflows.
agents-last-exam-1-1.input: A workplace task, tools and domain-specific software
agents-last-exam-1-1.output: A completed task artifact and application state
agents-last-exam-1-1.assessment: Task-specific verifiers assess the resulting work on the corresponding release.
agents-last-exam-1-1.date_note: October 14 commit explicitly pins the complete final 122-task v1.1 source tree. Earlier September 19 v1.1 assets and October 8 migrations existed before this frozen scope.

toolathlon-verified.description: Carry out long multi-application workflows using the final verified prompts, reference outcomes and evaluators.
toolathlon-verified.input: A task and an initialized software workspace
toolathlon-verified.output: Tool actions and a completed workspace task
toolathlon-verified.assessment: Task-specific scripts verify the outcome under the revised final release.

osworld-verified.description: The maintainers corrected task definitions, starting states and evaluators in the original computer-use benchmark. This named release is not an arbitrary verified submission.
osworld-verified.input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
osworld-verified.output: Actions that change application or system state
osworld-verified.assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.

osworld-2.description: A new long-horizon suite in realistic desktop environments. The first public V2 release pinned its task, asset and environment snapshots.
osworld-2.input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
osworld-2.output: Actions that change application or system state
osworld-2.assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.
osworld-2.date_note: Maintainer README explicitly announces launch June 26. The initial snapshot is named 2026.06.24; its name is not the announcement date. Untimed OSWorld 2.0 results do not identify which later snapshot was used.

osworld-2-2026-08-08.description: The August 2.0 snapshot revises task evaluators and website assets. The release notes identify both task hardening and fairness fixes; the VM images remain from June.
osworld-2-2026-08-08.input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
osworld-2-2026-08-08.output: Actions that change application or system state
osworld-2-2026-08-08.assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.

osworld-2-1.description: A named release with revised tasks, task assets, evaluation workflows and mocked websites. Frozen component versions define the score’s environment.
osworld-2-1.input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
osworld-2-1.output: Actions that change application or system state
osworld-2-1.assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.
osworld-2-1.date_note: Retain the offline-set or partial-set qualifier; those do not mean a full-suite result.

agent-arena.description: Compare agent components on real user work.
agent-arena.input: User requests and an instrumented agent environment.
agent-arena.assessment: Randomized component assignment estimates effects on observed outcome signals; it is not an ordinary preference vote.

toolarena.description: Turn a repository into a callable, testable tool.
toolarena.input: A software repository and function specification.
toolarena.output: A tool implementation in the task environment.
toolarena.assessment: Each task has its own tests of the implementation.

harness-arena.description: Give different coding-agent harnesses the same prompt and model. Human judges compare the resulting deliverables without knowing which harness produced them.
harness-arena.input: The same task prompt and reference material for both harnesses
harness-arena.output: Files or other deliverables requested by the task
harness-arena.assessment: Blind pairwise judgments feed the arena’s Elo ratings. This is a preference result, not a task pass rate.

ref-complexfuncbench.description: ComplexFuncBench: Exploring Multi-Step and Constrained Function Calling under Long-Context Scenario

ref-deepsearchqa.description: DeepSearchQA: Bridging the Comprehensiveness Gap for Deep Research Agents

ref-healthadminbench.description: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks

ref-physicianbench.description: PhysicianBench: Evaluating LLM Agents in Real-World EHR Environments

ref-screenspot-pro.description: ScreenSpot-Pro: GUI Grounding for Professional High-Resolution Computer Use
